_doc: Golden questions for hermes_eval.py. Each runs through `hermes chat -q` with the live config. truth = ground truth fetched at eval time (vision-mcp / Home Assistant) or fixed for anchored history; checks = what must hold. See docs/hermes.md 'Nightly eval'.

questions.why: Anchored history: the question that started this. Fails if routing, tags or date handling regress.
questions.prompt: Did the garbage truck come on the morning of Wednesday, November 11, 2026? If so, at what time?

truth.facts: Yes. A garbage truck passed the house on the street at 09:53-09:54 on Wednesday November 11 2026 (driveway camera).

checks.judge: The answer must say YES, the garbage truck came, at about 9:53-9:54 AM.

questions.why: Anchored history: a second vehicle kind, around midday rather than morning.
questions.prompt: Was a delivery van seen near the house around midday on Wednesday, November 11, 2026?

truth.facts: Yes. A delivery van (a UPS van per the camera description) was seen on the street at about 11:51 on Wednesday November 11 2026.

checks.judge: The answer must say YES, a delivery van was seen, at about 11:51 AM.

questions.why: Live: 'last time X' must come from the tag sightings, with the right day and time.
questions.prompt: When did the garbage truck last come by?

questions.why: Anchored negative: an honest 'no' (or yes, if the data says so) instead of padding with nearby sightings from other days.
questions.prompt: Did the cameras see a school bus on Sunday, November 8, 2026?

checks.judge: The answer's yes/no must match the ground truth for Sunday November 8 specifically. Mentioning a sighting on another day is fine only if it is clearly labelled as another day.

questions.why: Live: the caption timeline turned into a short narrative without inventing events.
questions.prompt: What did the cameras see yesterday? Give me a short summary.

checks.judge: PASS if the answer describes at least one specific event that appears in the ground-truth entries and states nothing that contradicts them or is absent from them. If the ground truth reports the archive is behind (archive_processed_until), the answer should mention that coverage is incomplete. If there are no entries at all, an answer saying it found nothing notable passes.

questions.why: Live: night window resolution ('last night' = 21:00-07:00) and honesty about quiet nights.
questions.prompt: Anything on the cameras last night?

checks.judge: PASS if the answer is consistent with the ground-truth entries for last night: it mentions at least one real entry when there are some, or says nothing notable happened when there are none. It must not invent events.

questions.why: Knows the vision worker archive is primary and Frigate is the live trigger.
questions.prompt: In two sentences: what's the difference between Frigate and the vision worker, and which one is the main source for questions about past camera activity?

truth.facts: Frigate watches the streams live and triggers events/alerts. The vision worker re-analyzes full-resolution footage (plus its own sweep of the recordings), keeps the archive with tags and descriptions, and is the main source for past activity.

checks.judge: PASS if the answer says the vision worker / its archive is the main source for past activity and Frigate is the live/real-time detector. FAIL if it says Frigate is the main source for history.

questions.why: Routing: live device state comes from Home Assistant, not the camera archive.
questions.prompt: Is the garage door open or closed right now?

questions.why: Routing + window: aircraft come from the radio logs (never cameras/HA), and 'last hour' means the last hour — the first dry run (2026-11-12) routed right but reported planes from 11 PM-2:35 AM as 'the last hour' at 19:20.
questions.prompt: What aircraft flew over the house in the last hour?
